This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management, all in one place.
No matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman. Hurricane Isaias made landfall Friday night near Destin, Florida.
Storm surge risk is going to be all across the Panhandle. This is very, very important.
There have been evacuation orders issued in a lot of the counties within the Panhandle, Zones A and B, which is essentially your barrier islands and low-lying areas in RV parks.
Hopefully many of you and most of you have heeded those evacuation orders.
Jared Perdue is with the Florida Division of Emergency Management. He says the Category 2 hurricane is bringing a life-threatening surge of as much as 9 feet along the Gulf Coast.
Most at risk is the Gulf Islands National Seashore. More than 600,000 homes now are without power in Florida and Alabama.
Hurricane Simon, meanwhile, has strengthened to a Category 2 storm and is heading toward Mexico's coast this weekend.
On Friday, the storm's maximum sustained winds increased to almost 100 miles an hour. A hurricane warning has been issued for parts of Mexico's central and southwest coasts.
Ukraine's President Vladimir Zelensky says the White House's decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel will only prolong the war.
As NPR's Joanna Kikisis reports, President Trump announced the deal Friday after speaking by phone with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Trump's decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel is the White House's latest attempt to lower fuel prices, which have risen sharply since the U.S. war on Iran.
In a voice message to reporters, Zelensky slams Trump's decision as weak and says Russia will make billions.
"That means more money for this war, more money to inflict suffering on us," he said. "It only feeds Putin and gives him the ability to keep fighting."
Ukraine's negotiating team is in Florida trying to restart peace talks. Zelensky says the team is being used as, quote, "a smokescreen."
Joanna Kikisis, NPR News, Cave.
President Trump has ordered a White House hearing next month to consider allegations of mortgage fraud against Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook.
As NPR's Scott Horsley reports, critics have dismissed that move as a kangaroo court.
The Supreme Court blocked President Trump's earlier effort to fire Lisa Cook, noting the Fed is supposed to be insulated from political pressure and finding that Trump had not given Cook an opportunity to defend herself.
Now, the president has set up a committee and ordered a hearing to weigh charges from a Trump loyalist that Cook made false statements on mortgage applications.
Cook's lawyers say the Fed official welcomes a chance to clear her name, but add they have grave doubts that the "hearing" will be legitimate.
The top Democrat on the Senate committee that oversees the Fed labeled the hearing a "show trial" and called it part of a dangerous quest by the president to illegally take over the nation's central bank.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
And you're listening to NPR News.
President Trump Friday named Katie Zachariah to the post of White House Press Secretary.
As he often does, he announced her appointment on social media.
Zachariah has been a communications advisor for Trump's media company and a conservative commentator on Fox News and Newsmax.
Earlier this year, she was a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security.
An Arizona congressional candidate told police she was raped by an unknown attacker in August while repairing a damaged campaign sign from member station KJZZ Cameron Sanchez reports.
Bernadette Green-Placentia initially didn't want to report she was raped.
She says she didn't want to think about it.
But the Democrats says it was important to speak up on behalf of other survivors of sexual violence, many of whom, she says, have reached out to her this week.
Still, Green-Placentia says the publicity has been difficult.
My world exploded again and now it's kind of come back.
And with that is, you know, the anger and the frustration that, you know, there's not actually anything I can do.
I wish I could just go find these people myself and haul them to jail or something.
Green-Placentia says she hasn't received any updates from the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office on their investigation.
For NPR News, I'm Cameron Sanchez in Phoenix.
Angel Rees scored 22 points Friday night as the Atlanta dream beat the New York Liberty 85 to 83.
They now advanced to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013.
They've never won a championship.
The four-seated dream swept the three-game series and if not lost in the postseason this year,
they'll face the winner of Las Vegas Golden State series when the WNBA Finals begin on October 17th.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
